FOREWORD
This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Crop Protection Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. A number of Indian Standard specifications for manually-operated sprayers have been formulated. These standards i ncludcd requirements and their methods of tests. Most of the tests were common to most of the sprayers. With a view to unify and to avoid repetition as well as to provide an easy reference, it was found de-irable to publish this standard. This standard was first published in 19R2. This first latest developments in the field.

revision has been brought to incorporate the

While preparing this standard, due consideration has been gi ven to the methods of tests stipulated in Equipment for Vector Control published by World Health Organization and also to the work done at Mechanical Engineering Research and Development Organization ( CSIR ), Ludhiana.

In reporting the result of a te~t or analyst < made in accordance with this standard, if the final value. observed or calculated, i'i to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised f.

1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes methods of tests for the
following manually-operated sprayers/pumps: a) Compression knapsack sprayers, non-pressure retaining type; b) Knapsack sprayer, piston type; c) Foot sprayer; d) Rocker sprayer; e) Stirrup type sprayer; and t) Atomizer type spra yer. c) Spray throw (see 6.5), and f) Spray coverage (see 6.6).

k) Frame, piston rod, pcdal lever or handle lever and extension (see 7.8); 01) Valve assembly (see 7.9); n) Tank impact (see 7.10); and p) Tank fatigue (see 7.11).

The sprayers/pumps for certification or for commercial test report shall he selected by the certifiying or testing authorities from production lot. The sprayers/pumps shall be new and shall be in a condition generally offered for sale. For confidential test report, the manufacturers may submit the sample to testing authority. The manufacturer shall supply all the relevant infonuation necessary [or conducting the test.

5 GENERAL TESTS
S.I Visual Examination
The equipment shall he visually examined with respect to tbe requirements given in the relevant Indian Standard. Conformity or otherwise of the requirements shall be reported.

3.2 Running-in
In order to overcome variation in initial performance, the sprayer/pump may be run-in before start of actual test. The lubrication and adjustments of the components shall be done in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations.

S.2

Checkin~

of Dimensions

Dimensional requirements given in the n-lcvanr lndian
Standard sball he measured and reported. Conformity or otherwise of the dimensions shall also he reported.

S.3

Cheekln~

of Material of Construction

4 TESTS
4.1 Relevant tests/observations; from the following, shall be made in a particular sprayer/pump:

4.1.1 General Tests (see 5) a) Visual examination (see 5.1), b) Checking of dimensions (see 5.2), and c) Checking of material of construction (see 5.3). 4.1.2 Performance Tests (see 6) a) Discharge rate (see 6.1), h) Volumetric efficiency (see 6.2), c) Pressure development (see 6.3), d) Leakage (see 6.4),

The inner diameter of the pump cylinder sbalJ he measured below the hell mouth of the cylinder. 6.2.2.1 The length of nne storkc shall he measured by subjecting the pump to a pressure of 30n kPa within a fluctuation of � 20 percent. 6.2.3 Divide the value obtained in 6.2.1 hy the value obtained ill 6.2.2 anJ t'xprl'ss the result in percentage.

7.1 Test for Leakage and Deformation of Pressure Chamber, Pump Cylinder and Pressure Tank 7.1.1 Pneumatic Test
A hose shall he attached to the opening of the pressure chamber or pump cylinder or tank. In case there arc a number of openings, other than the one to which the hose is attached shall he scaled. The pressure chamber or pump cylinder or tank shall then he pneumatically pressurized to a minimum of one and a half times the normal working pressure ol'thc sprayer and the pressure shall be retained for a period of one minute. The component shall be disconnected, immersed in water and examined for any leakage and deformation. 7.1.1.1 The pressure chamber or pump cylinder or tank shall be deemed to have passed this test if no leakage or deformation is found during this lest.

6.3.6 The above test shall he rcpr.. ated for a minimum
of four times and avrage value reported.

6.4 Test for Leakage
6.4.0 This test shall he: conducted for atomizer sprayer. 6.4.1 The piston assembly and removed.
stopper shall hl~

6.4.2 The outlet of the sprayer and the reservoir tiller hole shall he scaled.

6.4.3 A hose shall he attached to the opening of the pump cylinder and he pneumatically pressurized to an internal pressure of 34 kPa.
6.4.4 The pressure shall be retained for a period of 2 minutes and the sprayer is immersed in water.

7.1.2 Hydraulic Test
With the similar connection as tbat of7.1.1, the pressure chamber or pump cylinder or tank shall he pressurized to a static hydraulic pressure of a minimum of two and a half times the normal working pressure of the sprayer and the pressure shall he retained for a period of one minute. The pressure cha tuber or pump cylinder or tank :-,httlJ lx- examined for any leakage or deformation. 7.1.2.1 The pressun~ chamber or pump cylinder or tank shall he deemed to have passed this test if no leakage or deformation is found during the test.

6.4.5 During this test, sprayer shall not show any sign
of leakage or oozing.
